newsitem.title: DENMARK: BA to cut internal Danish Copenhagen - Aarhus route.
newsitem.headline: BA to cut internal Danish Copenhagen - Aarhus route.

text.p: British Airways Express is to end flights from Denmark's capital to the second city of Aarhus from April 14 because it expects a new high speed rail connection to hit air traffic.

In a statement received by Reuters on Friday, British Airways Express -- a franchise operated in Denmark by Sun Air -- said that it would instead improve other domestic services and open new international routes from provincial airports.
Denmark consists of the Jutland peninsula, on the European mainland, and several islands, chief among them the eastern island of Zealand on which Copenhagen is situated.
Road or rail travel between the country's two main cities has hitherto been slowed by a ferry crossing, making air travel, although expensive, attractive to those in a hurry.
But a new road and tunnel link has just been completed and passenger trains are to start running between the two cities from June 1.
